claim: R5-07 (a) amends R4-15 (a)'s reach: 'a field is a row's own path — a top-level key or a whole list'; inside a record the digest reads, 'an absent or unreadable sub-field takes its row's reading … at an absorb as at a creation and is compared as read'. V08 wrote it at §3.5's diff (l. 1681–1688), §2.4's lead (l. 628), §3.17 (l. 2632, 2710) and T-V8-61 (a) (a condition dropping `duration` clears its `untilWeek`; an institution returning `active` reopens). §7.7 item 10, the derivation table's index (base l. 12068), still restates R4-15 (a) unqualified: 'at an absorb a field that takes its fallback changes nothing, the carried fact standing (V08 §3.5)'. V08 notes a sub-field's fallback as one: §3.16 (8) (c) (l. 2611–2612) 'a headcount of 0 or less, or one that is no finite number, reads as none given, noted `field_fallback` with the field named'. By §7.7's words an absorb whose force headcount turns unreadable keeps the carried size; by V08 §3.5 it reads as none given and the look takes its next count. R5-07's sweep named V08's sites only. §7.7 cites V08 §3.5, which a port builder follows, so nothing built changes; the index is wider than its home.
required_change: §7.7 item 10 (base l. 12068): '— at an absorb a field that takes its fallback changes nothing, the carried fact standing (V08 §3.5);' → '— at an absorb a field that takes its fallback — a row's own path, a top-level key or a whole list — changes nothing, the carried fact standing, while a record's absent or unreadable sub-field is read by its row and compared, so the record follows what the dossier now says of it (V08 §3.5);'.

claim: §7.1's `bend.raised.underSpan` row (l. 10632; R5-02's D1 text) tests a hand carve against §4.3's crossing rule for ways: its cause is 'a ground `drawWay`, a moved way or a hand carve … crossing its under-deck strip where §4.3's crossing rule does not admit it', and its outcome 'the way or channel moved along the deck to cross under the nearest span that admits it'. §4.3's rule (l. 5643–5651) needs a clear width of at least 'the way's width + `clearWidthM`', a soffit meeting §2.7 *The clearance* 'for the crossed way', and a crossing within ± `squareDeg` of square. The home of the channel case is §2.7's support step (6) (b) (l. 2596–2599): a channel 'passes beneath where its crossing of the under-deck strip meets no part of the reservation'. §4.11's carve (l. 8238–8243) agrees with (6) (b). V09 §4.20.2 (4) (l. 3023–3025) restates §7.1 ('a carve across it crosses under the nearest span §4.3 admits'). Take a canal carved obliquely under a wide `open` span, touching no support. Under §2.7 and §4.11 it passes beneath. Under §7.1 no span admits it (moving along the deck does not change its angle), so it is cut at the strip's edges (`bend.raised.around`). Two units, two outcomes for one case. This is new this round: round 4's row tested a carve only against an `open` span.
required_change: §7.1's `bend.raised.underSpan` row, cause cell: 'a ground `drawWay`, a moved way or a hand carve meeting a standing raised way's supports, ramps, stairs, feet or a `vault` span's strip, or crossing its under-deck strip where §4.3's crossing rule does not admit it (§2.7's support step (6) (a)–(b))' → 'a ground `drawWay` or a moved way meeting a standing raised way's supports, ramps, stairs, feet or a `vault` span's strip, or crossing its under-deck strip where §4.3's crossing rule does not admit it (§2.7's support step (6) (a)), or a hand carve whose channel's crossing of that strip meets a support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span (§2.7's support step (6) (b))'. Outcome cell: 'the way or channel moved along the deck to cross under the nearest span that admits it (`bend.raised.underSpan`)' → 'the way moved along the deck to cross under the nearest span that admits it, the channel to the nearest crossing that meets none of these (`bend.raised.underSpan`)'; the rest of the cell stands. Second end, V09 §4.20.2 (4): 'and a ground road T4 `road` draws, a way moved or a carve across it crosses under the nearest span §4.3 admits, never over a support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span (`bend.raised.underSpan`), a road no span admits going round it (`bend.raised.around`).' → 'and a ground road T4 `road` draws or a way moved across it crosses under the nearest span §4.3 admits, and a carve's channel passes beneath where it meets no support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span, else moves along the deck to the nearest crossing that meets none — never over one (`bend.raised.underSpan`); a road no span admits goes round it, and a channel no crossing passes stops at the under-deck strip's edges (`bend.raised.around`).'. V09 §4.9's `bend.raised.underSpan` source cell takes §7.1's new cause and outcome words.

claim: This round's D4 text makes §5.3's gate row (l. 9257) read 'the roads leaving each walled stage (on ground part 0 or at a raised gate; …) equal its gate count (§4.2 S3 (7): its N main gates and any harbour gate placed)'. §4.8 *Gates* (l. 7655–7658) counts a raised gate as a main gate only 'where the arterial's raised way was created across the standing trace … so roads leaving each walled stage, so counted, = its gate count'. But a raised gate also stands where an elevated road is created across a ring: §4.8 l. 7668–7673 says 'at generation … an elevated road or aqueduct at S6's end across any ring; at an epoch V06 §3.19's founding', and §2.7's support step (3) agrees. An elevated road carries no arterial (§4.3 l. 5709–5714: `link`, joining two high wards, terraces, or a citadel and a great temple). Take a CITY whose elevated road joins a high ward inside a ring to one outside it. By §5.3 the elevated road is counted as a road leaving at a raised gate, yet that raised gate is neither one of the N main gates nor a harbour gate. The stage-end S7 check then fails on a lawful map, or builders differ on whether to count it.
required_change: §5.3's gate row, first parenthesis: '(on ground part 0 or at a raised gate; a deck passing over a stretch laid after its raised way is no crossing, §2.7's support step (6) (d))' → '(its arterials, on ground part 0 or at a raised gate where the arterial's raised way was created across the standing trace, §4.8 *Gates*; a raised gate whose raised way carries no arterial — an elevated road's — and a deck passing over a stretch laid after its raised way are no crossing of this count, §2.7's support step (3), (6) (d))'. The ≥ count's parenthesis stands.

claim: Before round 5, §2.7's support step (6) ended (`3310b53` l. 2615): "so a locked or pinned raised way is crossed as an unlocked one is (§7.4's lock column; T110-2)". R5-02's rewrite leaves only "A lock or pin holds the same" (base l. 2587), and §7.4's lock column says "its deck and piers held, as every raised way is from its creation" (l. 11403). Meanwhile §7.1's general row (l. 10587) refuses `refuse.locked` a map event that "crosses … a locked or pinned entity — a drawn way across a locked entity", and §7.2's test (l. 10815) refuses "a drawn way across a locked footprint". The `bend.raised.underSpan`/`bend.raised.around` row (l. 10632) and the `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l. 10631) say only "a standing raised way". So a ground `drawWay`, a moved way or a hand carve across a locked raised way matches both a refusal and a bend. T110-2 (4) (l. 18491–18500) runs the hand `drawWall` with the raised way locked and expects the bend, which settles walls. Neither T110-2 (5)'s hand roads (l. 18500–18503) nor T-V9-52 (V09 l. 4404) runs a lock. So one builder refuses the road and another bends it under a span or round the raised way, and both pass every bar.
required_change: 1. §7.1's lock row, cause: "— a drawn way across a locked entity," → "— a drawn way across a locked entity (but not a ground way, a carve or a wall stretch passing beneath a locked or pinned raised way's deck, which changes none of its parts and is bent by the `bend.raised.underSpan`, `bend.raised.around` and `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` rows as beneath an unlocked one: §2.7's support step (6), a lock or pin holds the same),". 2. `bend.raised.underSpan`'s row, cause: "meeting a standing raised way's supports" → "meeting a standing raised way's — locked, pinned or neither — supports"; `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s row: "across a standing raised way" → "across a standing raised way, locked, pinned or neither". 3. END (scope): T110-2 (5), after "a hand road wider than every `open` span's clear width drawn across one", add ", each hand road run again with the raised way locked and with it pinned — the same outcome, no `refuse.locked`".
